questions.prompt: When an order is placed, billing, shipping and analytics must each react to it. Which style fits?

options.text: A work queue, so one of the three services handles each order
Publish/subscribe, so every subscribing service gets the event
Direct synchronous calls from checkout to all three

questions.explanation: Each service needs every order, so each must get its own copy: that's pub/sub. A work queue would give each order to only one of them.

questions.prompt: Which are real benefits of putting a queue between checkout and the email service?

options.text: Checkout keeps working if the email service is down for a while
A burst of orders waits in the queue instead of overloading the email workers
Emails are guaranteed to be sent within 1 ms
Checkout responds without waiting for the email to be sent

questions.explanation: A queue decouples availability and absorbs bursts, and the producer doesn't wait. It adds delay rather than removing it.

questions.prompt: A worker charges a card, then crashes before acknowledging the message. The queue redelivers it. What prevents a double charge?

options.text: Making the consumer idempotent, for example by recording processed payment ids and skipping repeats

questions.explanation: At-least-once delivery will sometimes redeliver. An idempotent consumer makes the repeat harmless. At-most-once would avoid duplicates but could lose payments.

questions.prompt: One malformed message fails every time it's processed and is retried forever. What's the standard fix?

options.text: Delete the queue and recreate it
After a limited number of retries, move it to a dead-letter queue and alert someone

questions.explanation: Bounded retries with backoff, then a dead-letter queue, keep one bad message from blocking the rest. The alert makes sure someone fixes the cause and replays it.

questions.prompt: Messages arrive at 1,000 per second. Consumers process 800 per second. The queue has 50,000 messages now. What happens?

options.text: The queue drains in about 4 minutes
The backlog grows by 200 messages per second until consumers scale up or producers slow down

questions.explanation: Arrivals exceed processing by 200 per second, so the backlog grows without limit. A queue absorbs temporary bursts; a lasting gap needs more consumers, backpressure or shedding work.
